svg.title: M5 Core S3 Wiring
svg.desc: Wiring of MagicFocus on a CoreS3, which runs the MagicFocus firmware; the Module Gateway H2 runs TiltaBridgeH2. It is stacked between the CoreS3 and its DIN Base and talks to the CoreS3 over the M-Bus stack connector: G17 to the H2 RX, G10 from the H2 TX, G7 to its enable pin and G18 to its boot pin. The TFmini-S Lidar plugs into the DIN Base Port B, each wire named at both ends: 5V to 5V on red, GND to GND on black, the Lidar TX to G8 on green, and G9 to the Lidar RX on white. Port C on the DIN Base is not connected and must stay free because the H2 uses G18 and G17. The DIN Base also has a 500 mAh battery and a power switch, which cuts power to the CoreS3 and the H2; its 9 to 24 V DC input is optional and not connected. USB-C on the CoreS3 goes to the computer. The H2 reaches the Tilta Nucleus Nano II motor by radio on Tilta CH1, which is IEEE 802.15.4 channel 12. Below, an isometric exploded view from the back right shows the three modules pulled apart: the CoreS3 on top, its screen showing the MagicFocus page, which reads from the back because the firmware turns the display 180 degrees; the Module Gateway H2 in the middle; the DIN Base at the bottom. The H2 and the DIN Base each have 2 by 15 M-Bus pins along the same edge, which plug into the module above. Beside the stack, the TFmini-S Lidar is wired to the Port B plug by its green, white, red and black wires, and the Tilta Nucleus Nano II motor, standing on its rod clamp, has only a USB-C cable to a power supply, as the H2 reaches it by radio. On the back of the DIN Base, Port C is not connected, and the Lidar plug, with its green, white, red and black wires, goes into Port B.
svg.text: Stack the Gateway H2 between the CoreS3 and its DIN Base, and plug the Lidar into the DIN Base's Port B.
the switch cuts power to the CoreS3 and the H2
the H2 uses G18 and G17

g.text: Exploded and seen from the back right. The modules' 2 × 15 M-Bus pins plug into the one above, the Lidar's cable into Port B; the motor needs only power.
on top, showing the MagicFocus page
its cable plugs into Port B: G8, G9

svg.text: The H2 needs no wires on a CoreS3: its UART, enable and boot lines run through the M-Bus stack connector.
A Core2 is wired differently: Lidar on Port C, H2 on Port A.
